# complexipy

Blazingly fast cognitive complexity analysis for Python, written in Rust.

Installation • Quick Start • Features • Integrations • Learn More • Documentation • Changelog • Complexipy Teams

Scoring cognitive complexity of the Django codebase (2,929 files). Benchmarks

## Installation ```bash uv tool install complexipy # or uv add complexipy # or pip install complexipy ``` The `--diff`, `--diff-only`, and `--staged` options require Git 2.30 or newer on your `PATH`. Check your version with `git --version`. Git is not required for analysis without these options. ## What is Cognitive Complexity? > Cognitive complexity measures how hard a function's control flow is to follow. Use it to keep code easy to review and change, whether a person or an AI agent wrote it. These two functions have the same cyclomatic complexity, 4. Their cognitive complexity is different: ```python # Cognitive complexity: 3 def example1(a, b, c): if a: # +1 return 1 if b: # +1 return 2 if c: # +1 return 3 return 4 ``` ```python # Cognitive complexity: 6 def example2(a, b, c): if a: # +1 if b: # +2 (1 + nesting_level) if c: # +3 (1 + nesting_level) return 1 return 4 ``` Nested code makes the reader hold more context, so each nesting level adds to the score. complexipy implements the [Cognitive Complexity](https://www.sonarsource.com/resources/cognitive-complexity/) metric by G. Ann Campbell for Python. [How scores are calculated](https://complexipy.com/understanding-scores/) ## Quick Start

### Command Line ```bash # Analyze the current directory complexipy . # Set a custom threshold complexipy . --max-complexity-allowed 10 # Show failing functions with refactor suggestions complexipy . --failed --suggest-refactors # Save results to JSON complexipy . --output-format json # Block regressions against a git reference complexipy . --diff main # Exclude paths with glob patterns complexipy . --exclude "tests/**" ``` ### Python API ```python from complexipy import file_complexity # Analyze a file result = file_complexity("app.py") print(f"File complexity: {result.complexity}") for func in result.functions: print(f"{func.name}: {func.complexity}") ``` ## Features - **Cognitive complexity scores** that follow G. Ann Campbell's paper. [How scores work](https://complexipy.com/understanding-scores/) - **Gate only what a change makes worse**: `--diff` and `--staged` compare each function with a git reference. [Complexity diff](https://complexipy.com/diff-and-snapshots/#complexity-diff) - **Snapshot baselines**: record the current state of an existing codebase, then fail only on new or worse functions. [Snapshots](https://complexipy.com/diff-and-snapshots/#snapshot-baselines) - **Refactor suggestions and `--fix`**: rules such as guard clauses and extract helper, and automatic fixes where they are safe. [Refactoring rules](https://complexipy.com/refactoring-rules/) - **Output formats**: JSON, CSV, SARIF for GitHub code scanning, and GitLab Code Quality. [Output formats](https://complexipy.com/usage-guide/#output-formats) - **Language server**: inlay hints, hover, and warnings in VS Code, Neovim, and Zed. [Editor integration](https://complexipy.com/editors/) - **GitHub Action and pre-commit hook** for CI. [Integrations](#integrations) ## Common Questions **[How is complexity calculated?](https://complexipy.com/understanding-scores/)** Learn about the scoring algorithm, what each control structure contributes, and how nesting affects the final score. **[How does this compare to Ruff's PLR0912?](https://complexipy.com/comparison-with-ruff/)** Understand the key differences between cyclomatic complexity (Ruff) and cognitive complexity (complexipy), and why you might want to use both. **[Is this a SonarSource/Sonar product?](https://complexipy.com/about/)** No. complexipy is an independent project inspired by G. Ann Campbell's research, but it's not affiliated with or endorsed by SonarSource. ## Integrations
🔧 GitHub Actions ```yaml - uses: rohaquinlop/complexipy-action@v9 with: paths: . max_complexity_allowed: 10 output_json: true ```
🪝 Pre-commit Hook ```yaml repos: - repo: https://github.com/rohaquinlop/complexipy-pre-commit rev: v9.0.0 hooks: - id: complexipy ```
🧩 Editors Every editor uses `complexipy lsp`, a language server with inlay hints, hover, and warnings that update as you type. Install `complexipy` first (`uv tool install complexipy`). - **VS Code**: install the extension from the [Visual Studio Marketplace](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=rohaquinlop.complexipy) or [OpenVSX](https://open-vsx.org/extension/rohaquinlop/complexipy). - **Neovim and Zed**: see [Editor Integration](https://complexipy.com/editors/).
## Learn More - [Usage Guide](https://complexipy.com/usage-guide/) - installation, the basic CLI workflow, and troubleshooting - [Adopting in an Existing Codebase](https://complexipy.com/adoption/) - baseline, gate new code, then lower the threshold - [Configuration](https://complexipy.com/configuration/) - configuration files and the cache - [Diff and Snapshots](https://complexipy.com/diff-and-snapshots/) - complexity diff and snapshot baselines - [Ignores and Rule Selection](https://complexipy.com/ignores/) - inline ignores and rule selection - [CLI Options](https://complexipy.com/cli-reference/) - every CLI flag - [Editor Integration](https://complexipy.com/editors/) - the language server, inlay hints, and the VS Code, Neovim, and Zed setup - [API Reference](https://complexipy.com/api-reference/) - the complete Python API - [Understanding Scores](https://complexipy.com/understanding-scores/) - how the scoring algorithm works - [Comparison with Ruff](https://complexipy.com/comparison-with-ruff/) - cognitive vs cyclomatic complexity - [Refactoring Rules](https://complexipy.com/refactoring-rules/) - the rules behind `--suggest-refactors` - [Changelog](https://complexipy.com/changelog/) - what changed in each release ______________________________________________________________________
Inspired by the Cognitive Complexity research by G. Ann Campbell
